title: Man City vs. PSG Player Ratings: Superstar Forwards Light Up Champions League Classic
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayOct 14, 2026PSG edged an epic affair. / Martin Rickett/PA Images/Getty ImagesParis Saint-Germain ran out 4–2 winners during an utterly breathless Champions League classic with Manchester City on Wednesday.

The Cityzens had reveled in their role as pantomime villains during an emphatic win over Liverpool at the weekend, but a first home match since their damning guilty verdict for breaching the Premier League’s financial rules proved far less enjoyable. PSG produced one of the most complete first-half performances in recent Champions League history and deservedly boasted a three-goal halftime lead at the Etihad Stadium.

An astonishing move which started by PSG’s corner flag culminated in Désiré Doué firing an exquisite opener into the bottom corner, and the Frenchman turned provider two minutes later as he teed up Ousmane Dembélé’s far-post header. Vitinha proceeded to sweep home a pinpoint finish from the edge of the box to widen the advantage.

City came roaring back after halftime, though, creating an abundance of opportunities as they sought to stage an incredible turnaround. Erling Haaland scored either side of Maghnes Akliouche’s strike from range, but profligacy and a shocking first-half display ultimately proved costly for the home team.

Despite Ferran Torres missing a late penalty, PSG still clinched a second-successive European victory following their demolition of Slovan Bratislava last month. But for City, a first competitive defeat under Enzo Maresca leaves them with just three points from their league phase campaign so far.

PSG were unplayable during the first half at the Etihad. / Ryan Pierse/Getty ImagesThis was an otherworldly first-half performance from PSG as they tore the Premier League leaders to shreds on their own patch courtesy of some extraordinary attacking sequences. An emphatic reminder of why they remain the world’s best team.

City were pulled from pillar to post during a chastening 45 minutes. On every occasion, they pushed high up the field to press their visitors, who were bypassed with alarming ease and sent scuttling back toward their own goal with a sense of dread in the pit of their stomachs. Unfortunately for Enzo Maresca and his players, PSG were not in a merciful mood.
Each of their three goals were beautiful, with the first the pick of the bunch. An impeccable one-touch move from back to front eventually found Doué and, seconds later, the back of Donnarumma’s net.

The second was similarly well-worked as Doué, instead of firing another effort toward goal, dinked a delicate cross to Dembélé, who made no mistake from a tight angle as he nodded PSG further in front.

PSG’s third epitomized their swagger. Another awe-inspiring move ended up at the feet of Vitinha after Warren Zaïre-Emery’s audacious flick, and the midfielder calmly bent his shot into the near post to cap an electric spell.
It’s fair to say PSG’s first-half performance will live long in the memory.
City were well beaten on home soil. / Ryan Pierse/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*

GK: Gianluigi Donnarumma—5.4: Bruised by his former employers. Caught out at the near post by Doué for PSG’s opener and then endured an embarrassing moment as he ultimately parried Akliouche’s shot into his own goal. At least earned some redemption by saving Ferran Torres’s spot kick.
RB: Abdukodir Khusanov—5.8: Doué outsmarted him repeatedly throughout the first half, but Khusanov improved after moving to center back.
CB: Rúben Dias—5.5: Among the City defenders completely incapable of stifling a fearsome PSG forward line. Withdrawn at the break.
CB: Marc Guéhi—5.5: An evening to forget for Guéhi as PSG’s attack ran riot.
LB: Joško Gvardiol—7.1: Coped relatively well with Maghnes Akliouche, yet found it much tougher to handle Achraf Hakimi’s overlapping runs.
CM: Elliot Anderson—6.7: Often outnumbered by PSG’s classy three-man midfield. Received more support once Ayyoub Bouaddi entered the fray.
CM: Enzo Fernández—7.5: Readily involved in the final third as he spurned a huge chance and crashed the woodwork.
